name: Nonspecific Interstitial Pneumonia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ATS/ERS Consensus Classification for Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

criteria.description: Uniform interstitial inflammation and fibrosis without temporal heterogeneity on lung biopsy
High-resolution CT showing bilateral ground-glass opacities with reticular abnormalities and absence of honeycombing
Exclusion of other known causes of interstitial lung disease such as connective tissue disease or drug toxicity
Subacute to chronic dyspnea and cough lasting weeks to months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of NSIP pattern plus compatible HRCT findings and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Surgical lung biopsy is often required for definitive diagnosis; multidisciplinary discussion recommended.

laboratory: Autoimmune serologies usually negative but may be positive in secondary NSIP
imaging: HRCT showing bilateral ground-glass opacities predominantly in lower lobes
other: Histopathology demonstrating uniform interstitial inflammation and fibrosis without temporal heterogeneity

distinguishingFeatures: UIP pattern with temporal heterogeneity and honeycombing on HRCT and biopsy
Presence of organizing pneumonia pattern on biopsy
Systemic symptoms such as arthritis or rash
May have NSIP pattern but with clinical context

redFlags: Acute exacerbation with new bilateral infiltrates
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002
Nonspecific Interstitial Pneumonia: Clinical Features and Outcomes, Chest. 2013
Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias: Diagnosis and Treatment, Lancet Respir Med. 2017
